title: Loops + Functions
summary: Call functions inside loops — this is where functions become genuinely powerful.

content.title: The Combination
content.summary: Calling a function inside a loop repeats the whole action automatically.
content.body: You know loops repeat code. You know functions are reusable actions. Combine them:
content.note:
**Output:**
```
Legs bend...
Jump!
Landing!
Legs bend...
Jump!
Landing!
Legs bend...
Jump!
Landing!
```

Three full jump actions — from just two lines of calling code.

content.title: Passing the Loop Variable
content.summary: Pass `i` into a function to make each call slightly different.
content.body: You can pass `i` into the function so each round is labelled:
content.note:
**Output:**
```
--- Round 1 ---
You attack!
The enemy strikes back.
--- Round 2 ---
...
```

Every iteration passes a different number, so every round looks unique.

content.title: Why This Is Better Than a Big Loop
content.summary: If you want to change the battle action, you only update the function — not every loop.
content.body:
Imagine the battle action needs to change. Without functions, you'd edit the code inside every loop.

With functions, you update `battle_round()` once — and every loop call automatically gets the new version.

This is called **separation of concerns**: the loop decides *how many times*, the function decides *what happens*.

content.title: Multiple Functions in One Loop
content.summary: A loop can call several different functions in sequence, building complex repeated scenes.
content.body: A single loop iteration can call several functions:
content.note: This builds a three-room walk-through with almost no repetition in the calling code.

steps.instruction: Step 1: Inside `dance_move(step)`, replace `pass` with one indented `print()` line that uses `step`. For example: `print("Step", step, "— spin!")`. Save — nothing should print yet (no calls).
steps.starterCode:
# A labelled dance move
def dance_move(step):
    pass

# Loop through 5 steps

steps.instruction: Step 2: Add a second indented `print()` line inside `dance_move()` for flair — something like `print("The crowd cheers!")`.

Step 3: Below the function (no indent), add a `for` loop: `for i in range(1, 6):`. Inside the loop (indented 4 spaces), call `dance_move(i)`. Run it. You should see steps 1 through 5, each with the crowd cheering.

bonusSteps.instruction: Bonus: Add a second function called `big_finish()` that prints a grand finale message. After the loop ends (no indent again), call `big_finish()` once.

progressiveHints: Replace `pass` with two `print` lines. Use the `step` parameter: `print("Step", step, "— spin!")`.
Add a second line for flair, like `print("The crowd cheers!")`.
